scenario: A government science funding agency only tracks research grants above $50,000 in its public transparency database. A policy analyst uses the database to estimate the average grant size to argue for budget reallocation.

data.description: Database only records grants > $50,000. All grant sizes assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $40,000.

question: The transparency database shows a mean grant of $95,000. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean grant size Î¼ across ALL grants awarded by the agency, and (b) the fraction of grants that are tracked in the database.
naive_answer: The true mean grant size is approximately $95,000 since that is the database figure.
naive_trap: About 23% of grants fall below the $50,000 tracking threshold and are invisible in the database. The true agency mean is about $16,000 lower. A policy analyst using $95,000 would overestimate total funding obligations and mischaracterise the distribution of research support.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(50000-mu)/40000; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+40000*norm.pdf(a)/sf-95000 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,10000,94999)
assert abs(mu-78959)<600
assert abs(norm.sf((50000-mu)/40000)-0.7655)<0.01
